results.title: AI for Postoperative Pain and Opioid Stewardship in Pediatric Surgery: A Systematic Review
results.authors: Shamsi, Atefeh
results.journal: Pain management nursing : official journal of the American Society of Pain Management Nurses
results.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To synthesize evidence on artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled postoperative pain assessment and prediction, opioid-related risk prediction, patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) monitoring, and implementation considerations in pediatric surgical care. DESIGN: A systematic review with narrative synthesis of evidence concerning AI applications in pediatric postoperative pain management and opioid stewardship. DATA SOURCES: Biomedical, nursing, engineering, computer science, trial-registry, Google Scholar, and citation sources were systematically searched through March 2026. REVIEW/ANALYSIS METHODS: Eligible studies evaluated AI, machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, multimodal sensing, or AI-enabled tools in pediatric surgical or postoperative populations. A single reviewer performed study selection, data extraction, and methodological appraisal, with consultation from an external subject-matter expert. Risk of bias and applicability were assessed using design-appropriate appraisal tools. Findings were narratively synthesized because clinical and methodological heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis. RESULTS: Of 198 identified records, 137 were screened, and 20 full-text reports were assessed. Eleven studies were included in the qualitative synthesis, alongside one companion dataset report. Applications included automated pain assessment, home-based pain monitoring, prolonged opioid-use prediction, and prediction of pain or adverse effects during PCA. Most studies evaluated facial expressions using computer vision or multimodal combinations of physiological, video, and audio data. Reported performance varied substantially, with validation predominantly limited to internal datasets. No randomized trial or controlled clinical-impact study demonstrated reductions in pain intensity, opioid exposure or prescribing, adverse events, readmissions, or length of stay attributable to AI-guided care. CONCLUSIONS: AI-enabled tools show potential to support pediatric postoperative pain assessment and opioid-related risk stratification. However, current evidence is insufficient to justify routine clinical implementation. External validation, prospective clinical evaluation, fairness assessment, and workflow-integrated effectiveness studies are needed. NURSING PRACTICE IMPLICATIONS: AI-enabled assessment and prediction tools may complement pediatric nurses' clinical assessment, pain monitoring, opioid-related risk identification, patient and family education, and timely escalation of care. Nevertheless, their use should remain supplementary to professional nursing judgment until clinical effectiveness, safety, and generalizability are established.

results.title: Artificial Intelligence in Brain Arteriovenous Malformation Neuroimaging: A Scoping Review of Clinical Applications, Performance, and Translation Readiness
results.authors: de Oliveira, Jean G and Veiga, Raphael E and Guirado, Vinicius M P and Veiga, José Carlos E
results.journal: Journal of neuroradiology = Journal de neuroradiologie
results.abstract: BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI) is used in brain arteriovenous malformation (AVM) neuroimaging, but translation readiness remains incompletely mapped. PURPOSE: To characterize AI-related applications, reported performance, and barriers to clinical deployment. METHODS: We conducted a PRISMA-ScR-guided review of PubMed, Embase, and Google Scholar from inception through 20 December 2025, with PubMed additionally searched on 23 August 2026. Eligible sources addressed AI, machine learning, radiomics, or automated computational analysis of brain AVM imaging. Results were charted descriptively; heterogeneous metrics were not pooled. RESULTS: Thirty-two sources were included: 28 primary reports and four contextual evidence syntheses. Thirteen primary reports had a documented AI/ML component. Of these, seven used imaging-derived inputs only, three combined imaging with clinical or treatment predictors, one compared separate imaging and clinical models, and two had unresolved final predictor sets. Three nidus-segmentation reports gave Dice estimates of 0.754, 0.80 and 0.82; partition details were unavailable for the first, and the last applied to detected lesions. Validation designs and clinical targets varied, precluding a pooled performance estimate. CONCLUSION: AI/ML shows technical feasibility in selected brain AVM imaging and prediction tasks. Clinical benefit and routine deployment have not been demonstrated. Multicenter institutional validation, calibration, transparent reporting and prospective clinical-impact evaluation remain priorities.

results.title: Artificial intelligence-enabled interventions for smoking cessation: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
results.authors: Adebisi, Yusuff Adebayo and Alhur, Anas Ali and Ogunkola, Isaac Olushola and Olaoye, Damilola Quazeem and Ong, Christian Joseph N and Iyagbaye, Eseosa and Lucero-Prisno Iii, Don Eliseo
results.abstract: BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in digital smoking-cessation tools, but whether AI-enabled personalisation improves abstinence, and whether any benefit reflects the AI component rather than digital support more broadly, remain uncertain. OBJECTIVE: To systematically review and meta-analyse randomised controlled trials (RCTs) of AI-enabled smoking-cessation interventions using an explicit operational framework that distinguished learning, inference and substantive language-understanding components from conventional fixed-rule automation. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and the Web of Science Core Collection were searched from inception to 7 August 2026 without language, date, publication-status or study-design filters; Cochrane CENTRAL, ClinicalTrials.gov and the WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform were searched, and backward and forward citation searching was undertaken, on 21 October 2026. Eligible studies were RCTs in adults who smoked combustible cigarettes in which an AI-enabled component materially generated, selected, personalised, adapted, predicted, recommended or timed cessation support. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data and assessed risk of bias using RoB 2; disagreements were resolved by a third reviewer. Risk ratios (RRs) were pooled using random-effects restricted maximum likelihood models with Knapp-Hartung adjustment, separately for abstinence at the longest follow-up of at least six months (primary) and at approximately three months (secondary). Exploratory sensitivity analyses were restricted to biochemically verified abstinence, and further analyses examined missing-data assumptions, completeness of AI reporting and results available only in trial registries. Certainty of evidence was assessed using GRADE. RESULTS: Fourteen RCTs involving 101,331 randomised participants were included, eight of which contributed to meta-analysis. AI functions comprised message recommender systems (five trials), conversational agents (three trials), wearable-sensor smoking-detection models (three trials), lapse-risk prediction models applied to ecological momentary assessments (two trials) and one app described as AI-enabled without technical detail. Pooled abstinence at six months or longer was RR 1.33 (95 % CI 0.82-2.15; I-squared = 67.6 %; four trials, 2,694 participants), and at approximately three months RR 1.36 (95 % CI 0.63-2.93; I-squared = 58.4 %; four trials, 715 participants). Exploratory analyses restricted to biochemically verified abstinence yielded RR 1.53 (95 % CI 1.07-2.19; three trials, 1,207 participants) at six months or longer and RR 2.03 (95 % CI 1.03-4.03; three trials, 366 participants) at approximately three months; these analyses changed the composition of the evidence set by excluding the largest null trials and should not be interpreted as confirmatory. Adding two completed trials whose results were available only in a trial registry moved the six-month estimate towards the null (RR 1.20, 95 % CI 0.91-1.59). In an exploratory comparison by comparator architecture, point estimates more consistently favoured AI-enabled packages versus usual or minimal care than versus active non-AI digital comparators, where results were inconsistent; however, comparator type was confounded with other trial characteristics. Certainty of evidence ranged from low to very low. No included trial randomised a generative large language model intervention. CONCLUSIONS: Randomised evidence for AI-enabled smoking cessation remains sparse, heterogeneous and imprecise. AI-containing packages may improve abstinence when added to usual or minimal care, but current trials do not establish a consistent incremental benefit of AI over well-designed non-AI digital support. Larger trials with biochemically verified long-term endpoints, matched comparators that isolate the algorithmic contribution, and transparent AI-specific reporting are needed before superiority of AI-enabled cessation support can be inferred.

results.title: Artificial intelligence in healthcare: clinical applications, evidence maturity, risks, and life-cycle governance
results.authors: León-Figueroa, Darwin A and Acosta-Porzoliz, Renzo and Cómina-Tamayo, María Julia and Aguirre-Milachay, Edwin and Vera-Ponce, Víctor Juan and Valladares-Garrido, Mario J
results.abstract: BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used across clinical, administrative, and public health settings, but technical performance alone does not establish clinical utility, safety, equity, or sustainability. OBJECTIVE: To critically analyze contemporary healthcare AI applications, characterize source types and non-ordinal evidence profiles in the supporting literature, synthesize key opportunities and risks, and identify governance requirements for clinically useful, safe, equitable, and responsible implementation. METHODS: We conducted a critical narrative synthesis using PubMed, the Virtual Health Library, Web of Science, and Scopus as source-discovery tools on July 16, 2026. A curated corpus of 28 bibliographically verifiable publications was assembled judgmentally to provide complementary coverage of clinical applications, evidence characteristics, implementation, risk, and life-cycle governance. Sources were classified by primary design and non-mutually exclusive evidentiary domains, and the evidence described within them was characterized using non-ordinal profile categories. Findings were synthesized qualitatively because of substantial heterogeneity across technologies, settings, and source designs. RESULTS: The curated corpus addressed diagnosis and imaging, prediction and monitoring, clinical documentation, conversational systems, public health, hospital operations, and specialty applications. Within this assembled corpus, technical-performance/validation and process-utility/workflow domains were represented more often than clinical or patient-safety outcomes, economic outcomes, or post-deployment surveillance; these document-level counts are descriptive and have no inferential weight beyond the selected sources. Reported or proposed benefits included diagnostic support, personalization, documentation, surveillance, and workflow efficiency. Recurrent risks included poor generalizability, bias, miscalibration, hallucinations, opacity, privacy concerns, interoperability problems, inappropriate automation, unclear accountability, and hidden costs. CONCLUSIONS: Within this non-exhaustive corpus, the evidence more consistently supported assistive, context-specific uses than generalized autonomous replacement. Responsible implementation requires a clearly defined intended use, governed data, contextual validation, risk-proportionate human oversight, traceability, equity and safety assessment, continuous monitoring, and procedures to restrict, suspend, or withdraw systems when performance or implementation conditions change.

results.title: Comparison of a quantitative MRI-based radiomics marker with semiquantitative signal alteration scores in the infrapatellar fat pad: Data from the Osteoarthritis Initiative
results.authors: Marth, Adrian A and Ziegeler, Katharina and Joseph, Gabby B and Liu, Felix and Zwerin, Romy and Lynch, John A and Lane, Nancy E and McCulloch, Charles E and Nevitt, Michael C and Link, Thomas M
results.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To develop a quantitative MRI-based radiomics marker of the infrapatellar fat pad (qIPFP) based on semiquantitative IPFP signal alteration scores (sqIPFP), and to evaluate whether its associations with symptoms and imaging features of knee osteoarthritis are comparable to those of sqIPFP. DESIGN: This study included 2640 participants from the Osteoarthritis Initiative, split into training (n = 2112) and test (n = 528) sets. Deep learning-based IPFP segmentation was performed on baseline intermediate-weighted fat-suppressed 3.0-Tesla MRI. Stability selection with bootstrap-resampled ElasticNet regression (≥80% selection frequency) identified radiomic features for qIPFP trained on a composite score combining sqIPFP size and intensity. Linear regression models, including age, sex, race, and body mass index as covariates, were used to compare qIPFP against the sqIPFP composite, size, and intensity scores for cross-sectional associations with the Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC) pain score and Whole-Organ Magnetic Resonance Imaging Score (WORMS) scores of cartilage lesions, meniscal lesions, and bone marrow lesions (BML). RESULTS: Forty stable features were included in the qIPFP marker, which showed adjusted R² values of 0.15 (95% CI 0.10-0.23) for WOMAC pain, 0.13 (95% CI 0.09-0.20) for cartilage lesions, 0.10 (95% CI 0.05-0.17) for meniscal lesions, and 0.08 (95% CI 0.05-0.14) for BML. There was no evidence of a difference compared to sqIPFP scores (all p ≥ 0.09), except for BML, where the sqIPFP composite (0.12, 95% CI 0.08-0.19; p = 0.042) and intensity scores (0.12, 95% CI 0.08-0.19; p = 0.038) yielded higher adjusted R². CONCLUSIONS: A quantitative radiomics marker of infrapatellar fat pad signal alterations showed cross-sectional associations with knee osteoarthritis symptoms and imaging features comparable to those of semiquantitative scoring except for bone marrow lesions, with the advantage of fully automated, reader-independent assessment.

results.title: Artificial Intelligence in Cleft and Craniofacial Care
results.authors: Mueller, Andreas A and Solenthaler, Barbara and Schnabel, Till N and Lill, Yoriko and Nalabothu, Prasad and Benitez, Benito K
results.journal: Oral and maxillofacial surgery clinics of North America
results.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into cleft and craniofacial care to facilitate objective assessment, optimize treatment planning, and improve outcome evaluation. By leveraging 3-dimensional imaging, machine learning, and automated workflows, AI addresses key clinical challenges such as anatomic variability, limited robust normative references, and reliance on subjective expertise. Recent developments enable streamlined data acquisition and automated design of surgical devices. This article reviews current applications and highlights clinically relevant advances toward integrated digital workflows and emerging digital twin concepts, with the goal of improving precision, efficiency, and accessibility across cleft and craniofacial treatment pathways.

results.title: A comprehensive review of emerging flexible tactile sensors: mechanisms, nanomaterials, microstructures and applications
results.authors: Li, Zhenyu and Zhang, Zekun and Zhou, Jianxin and Wang, Yaoming and Zhang, Xuang
results.abstract: Flexible tactile sensors represent pivotal physical interfaces for human-machine interaction and embodied intelligence. However, the inherent trade-offs between sensitivity and sensing range, multimodal crosstalk, and long-term biosafety remain critical bottlenecks hindering practical implementation. This work adopts a 'Material-Microstructure-Application' pipeline to categorize and analyze recent advancements developed in response to technical challenges. The review first delineates mainstream sensing mechanisms, followed by an analysis of the intrinsic physical properties and modification strategies of carbon/metal-based nanomaterials, emerging MXenes, and composite hydrogels. Specifically, a critical assessment of the biosafety and toxicological risks associated with functional nanomaterials in long-term wearable and implantable scenarios is conducted, bridging a notable gap from the perspective of clinical translation. Building upon these material foundations, the role of surface micro-engineering, consisting of biomimetic interlocking and porous architectures, in surpassing performance limits through the fine-tuning of contact mechanics is discussed. Furthermore, the potential of flexible manufacturing techniques, such as 3D printing and laser direct writing, to overcome the constraints in complex 3D architecting and scalable fabrication is summarized. Eventually, frontier applications in medical monitoring and robotic perception are exhibited, with a focus on the empowerment of machine learning-assisted signal classification, multimodal recognition, and inverse design. This review aims to provide comprehensive theoretical insights for the development of next-generation tactile sensing systems characterized by high biocompatibility and spatiotemporal resolution.

results.title: EETANet: A Human-Centered Intelligent Framework for Exercise Posture Quality Assessment
results.authors: Hassan, Esraa and Samy Talaat, Amira and Aleryani, Aliya and Albelaihi, Rana and Elsabagh, M A
results.abstract: As physical rehabilitation and fitness monitoring increasingly shift toward autonomous and home-based healthcare, accurate and intelligent posture assessment systems have become essential for supporting personalized rehabilitation and clinical decision making. This study proposes the Edge-Enhanced Temporal Attention Network (EETANet), a human-centered ambient intelligence framework for automated exercise posture assessment and quality evaluation. The proposed framework is designed as an end-to-end computational pipeline that transforms raw multivariate motion signals into posture quality predictions using a compact set of core biomechanical posture features. The pipeline integrates data preprocessing, signal enhancement, multi-domain feature representation, and deep neural classification to capture the relevant spatial and temporal characteristics of human movement. Signal preprocessing incorporates data cleaning, z-score normalization, and Savitzky-Golay smoothing to improve signal quality while preserving temporal dynamics. Subsequently, informative posture representations are extracted through complementary temporal, spectral, and morphological descriptors, enabling the model to characterize motion variations associated with posture quality. These representations are learned using a Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) classifier within the proposed EETANet framework to model nonlinear relationships between posture features and quality levels. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that the compact five-feature configuration achieves an accuracy of 90.83%, precision of 90.99%, recall of 90.83%, and F1-score of 90.84%. Notably, this compact configuration outperforms the corresponding 24-feature MLP configuration, which achieves 88.83% accuracy, indicating that a reduced set of core posture features can provide effective discriminative information while avoiding unnecessary feature redundancy. These findings demonstrate the potential of EETANet as an efficient framework for automated posture quality assessment in rehabilitation, fitness monitoring, and ambient healthcare applications.

results.title: [Multimodal assessment of lower limb muscle fatigue and variable stiffness impedance control method for exoskeletons]
results.authors: Li, Ruigang and Zhang, Bi and Li, Jiwei and Feng, Jun and Bao, Ruilai and Zhang, Tingfeng and Zhang, Liang and Zhao, Xingang
results.journal: Sheng wu yi xue gong cheng xue za zhi = Journal of biomedical engineering = Shengwu yixue gongchengxue zazhi
results.abstract: Aiming at the problems of insufficient real-time human-computer interaction and limited fatigue monitoring of lower limb rehabilitation exoskeleton, a multi-modal evaluation of lower limb muscle fatigue and exoskeleton variable stiffness impedance control method are proposed. This method extracts the characteristics of surface electromyography time-frequency domain and A-mode ultrasound muscle thickness, combines ventilation and subjective fatigue scale, and uses support vector machine to construct a five-classification model of fatigue level to achieve state evaluation. In addition, this study further designs a variable stiffness impedance control strategy to dynamically adjust the exoskeleton parameters in real time according to the muscle state to improve the interaction safety. Experiments show that the classification accuracy of the multi-modal fusion model proposed in this study is 92.30%, and the system delay is less than 200 ms. In the walking test, the variable stiffness control strategy can further significantly reduce the net respiratory metabolic rate of the user compared with no exoskeleton or under built-in control assistance of exoskeleton. The method proposed in this paper realizes effective fatigue assessment and adaptive assistance, and provides a new idea for intelligent interaction of lower limb rehabilitation robots.

results.title: Role of Artificial Intelligence in Radiation Oncology: A Missed Opportunity for LMICs?
results.authors: Siddiqui, Hiba and Aliyeva, Turkan and Khan, Agha Muhammad Hammad and Khan, Laraib and Jangda, Abdul Qadir and Mansha, Atif and Tsang, Derek S
results.journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics
results.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) are driving a major shift in modern medicine, particularly within radiation oncology. AI in radiation oncology offers low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) a way to offset critical shortages of oncologists and physicists by automating segmentation, planning, and quality checks, improving efficiency, and expanding equitable access to care. Its actual value depends on validation against LMICs' infrastructure and patient populations, an area where current evidence remains limited. This review aims to comprehensively summarize the current evidence on AI and ML applications across key domains of radiotherapy, while highlighting global disparities in adoption, particularly in LMICs. METHODOLOGY: This critical review conducted a comprehensive literature search across PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library for studies published between 2010 and April 2026. Only relevant studies emphasizing the efficiency of AI in radiation workflow and the existing gaps in its adoption within LMICs were included in this review. RESULTS: Eleven studies published between 2019 and 2025 were included. Study designs comprised original research (n=5), reviews (n=4), a survey (n=1), and a study protocol (n=1). Studies were conducted across multiple LMICs in Africa, Asia, and Latin America, predominantly evaluating AI-based contouring and treatment-planning tools, with Radiation Planning Assistant (RPA) being the most frequently reported platform. AI tools demonstrated comparable performance in LMICs relative to High-Income Countries (HICs), particularly with regard to time efficiency and the quality of target volume contouring. Yet the majority of LMICs still don't have AI tools in their radiation centers to work efficiently. CONCLUSION: The current literature reveals a gap between the need for AI in radiation oncology in LMICs and the available evidence supporting its implementation. LMICs could benefit substantially from AI-enabled improvements in radiation oncology. Several conclusions about the applicability of these findings in LMIC settings were drawn by extrapolation from studies conducted in HIC contexts, which substantially limits their direct generalizability to lower-resource environments. Cost-effective and accessible AI models hold promise to address workforce shortages, improve efficiency, and expand equitable access to quality radiotherapy services.

results.title: Implementation of an AI-Triggered Rapid Response - Association with Mortality
results.authors: Nahass, Thomas A and Hanna, Joseph S and Liu, Nancy and Martinez, Nicole and Halm, Ethan A and Rockman, Amy and Roy, Jason and Gilligan, Christopher and Murtha, Amy P and Gracias, Vicente and Anderson, Ruric Andy and O'Mahony, Stephen P
results.abstract: BACKGROUND: Use of a real-time, machine learning-enabled clinical deterioration prediction model combined with an automated rapid response team (RRT) activation could reduce inpatient mortality. The objective was to assess reduction in risk-adjusted inpatient mortality following implementation of the Epic Deterioration Index (EDI) combined with an automated RRT activation in a large regional health system. METHODS: We conducted a quasi-experimental, staggered cohort study using a pre- versus postimplementation design. The setting was a regional health system with 11 acute care hospitals including academic, community teaching, and nonteaching facilities. Participants included adult medical-surgical admissions with an EDI greater than or equal to 60 from October 1, 2022, to August 30, 2024. We evaluated the clinical impact of deploying real-time, targeted electronic health record (EHR) alerts and RRT push notifications; the primary outcome was risk-adjusted inhospital mortality. RESULTS: The study included 23,132 patients. Mean age was 71.9 years, 51.6% were male, and 51.4% were non-Hispanic white. In total, 10,803 patients (46.7%) were preintervention and 12,329 (53.3%) were postintervention; 5746 postintervention encounters (46.6%) generated a push notification to the RRT, although not all resulted in RRT activation. The postintervention group compared with the preintervention group was associated with increased RRT activations (37.5% vs. 25.3%; absolute difference, 12.2 percentage points [95% confidence interval (CI), 11.0 to 13.4]; adjusted odds ratio, 1.74 [95% CI, 1.61 to 1.88]) and decreased unadjusted inhospital mortality (18.6% vs. 23.1%; absolute difference, -4.5 percentage points [95% CI, -5.6 to -3.5]), without a significant increase in escalations of care (1.1% vs. 1.0%; absolute difference, 0.1 percentage points [95% CI, -0.18 to 0.37]; adjusted odds ratio, 1.34 [95% CI, 0.97 to 1.85]). Risk-adjusted odds of inhospital mortality, accounting for age, comorbidities, hospital type, EDI score, and clustering at the hospital level were lower in the intervention group (adjusted odds ratio, 0.82 [95% CI, 0.74 to 0.91]). CONCLUSIONS: Implementation of the EDI combined with RRT activation was associated with a reduction in risk-adjusted inpatient mortality across different types of hospitals in a large health system.

results.title: Towards Intelligent Membrane Systems: A Critical Analysis of Digital Twin-ML Integration for Real-Time Process Optimization, Fouling Management, and Autonomous Design
results.authors: Sadare, Olawumi O and Alonge, Samuel P and Akinyemi, Azeez G and Adesina, Abass A and Adesola-Olabiyi, Shukrah and Fajimi, Lanrewaju I
results.abstract: Membrane separation is central to potable water production, wastewater reclamation, desalination, gas separation, and decarbonization, yet its economics remain constrained by fouling and by a gap between process data and timely operating decisions. Digital twins (DTs) offer live, bidirectionally coupled virtual representations of physical assets, while machine learning (ML) extracts predictive and prescriptive insights from operational data. Together, they are promising computational approaches for membrane systems. However, their applications have largely evolved independently across fouling prediction, DT development, and ML-based materials discovery. This review argues that these are converging strands of a single trajectory toward self-sensing, self-predicting, and eventually self-designing membrane systems, and that treating them separately obscures key interdependencies. The contributions are threefold. First, applying the digital model/digital shadow/digital twin taxonomy, it shows that most published membrane DTs are digital shadows (DSs). Second, it proposes a five-level autonomy framework, inspired by vehicle automation taxonomies, providing a unified scale for comparing applications ranging from LSTM-based fouling forecasting and reinforcement learning dosing control to autonomous materials laboratories. Third, it integrates autonomous materials design, including self-driving laboratories, inverse design, generative models, and Bayesian search, into the upper levels of this ladder. Evidence is synthesized across reverse osmosis, nanofiltration, ultrafiltration, microfiltration, membrane bioreactors, membrane distillation, and gas separation membranes, with emphasis on critically assessing model performance and generalizability. The study concludes with a roadmap for overcoming data limitations, poor interpretability, interoperability gaps, cybersecurity risks, techno-economic barriers, and regulatory trust deficits that block autonomous membrane systems.

results.title: Triboelectric Nanogenerators for Human-Robot Motion Energy Harvesting and Sensing: Structures, Embodied Artificial Intelligence, and Self-Powered Applications
results.authors: Li, Jian and Yin, Gefan and Sun, Zhen and Li, Chenhao and Mo, Yadong and Gu, Cong and Zhang, Xiangyan and Wang, Sikai and Xu, Xiangjie and Liu, Runxiao and Wang, Jiahe and Chen, Pengyu and Li, Ziyang and Wei, Shimin
results.abstract: The rapid development of humanoid robots and embodied artificial intelligence (EAI) is accelerating the transformation of elderly care and rehabilitation toward interactive, adaptive, and personalized human-robot collaboration. In this context, motion sensing technology is of critical importance. Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs), which convert biomechanical motions into electrical signals, offer a promising route toward self-powered motion perception in embodied healthcare. This review summarizes recent advances in TENG-based multimodal motion sensing for human-robot interaction, covering inertial vibration sensing, tactile sensing, non-contact sensing, continuous trajectory sensing, and joint rotation sensing. The influences of structural configuration, motion mode, sensing direction, detection range, sensitivity, resolution, electrical output, and channel number on sensing performance under specific application scenarios are analyzed. Particular attention is paid to how TENG design strategies influence sensing universality, signal effectiveness, and the reliability of health monitoring and rehabilitation evaluation. Furthermore, the integration of TENGs with artificial intelligence (AI) technologies, including multimodal fusion, network architectures, edge computing, transfer learning, and large language models, is reviewed. Finally, applications in adaptive rehabilitation sensing, self-powered electrical stimulation, fully self-powered systems, and human‑robot interfaces are highlighted, offering perspectives on closed-loop "sensing-evaluation-regulation" frameworks for green, low-carbon EAI healthcare.

results.title: Machine Learning-Enabled Meta-Analysis of Bioengineering Micro- and Nanorobots
results.authors: Rahimi, Ehsan and Palacios-Corella, Mario and Rahimi, Mohammad and Mohutsiwa, Lucky Odirile and Puigmartí-Luis, Josep and Pané, Salvador
results.abstract: Micro- and nanorobots are emerging bioengineering tools for targeted delivery, biosensing, imaging, and minimally invasive therapy, yet systematic design and cross-study translation remain hindered by heterogeneous experimental conditions, inconsistent reporting, and sparse structured data sets. Here, we develop a literature-derived data set of micro- and nanorobot systems and apply artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled structural meta-analysis to resolve relationships among bioengineering constraints, actuation strategies, environmental conditions, measurement practices, and performance. Dendrogram- and correlation-based clustering identifies three dominant descriptor modules spanning deployment context, actuation-measurement coupling, and design intent. Supervised learning reveals structured descriptor patterns in propulsion mechanisms, whereas prediction of instantaneous velocity remains only moderately generalizable, highlighting substantial domain shift across materials, propulsion physics, biological media, operating conditions, and measurement protocols. Overall, AI and machine learning provide a powerful framework for mapping heterogeneous design landscapes, exposing reporting biases and descriptor coupling, and advancing standardized data sets for reliable comparison and predictive design.

results.title: Machine learning-driven development of food liposomes: phospholipid extraction, formulation design, preparation control, and stability prediction
results.authors: Li, Shuangshuang and Gouda, Mostafa and Ma, Xinxin and Isobe, Kazuhiro and Handa, Akihiro and Huang, Xi and Cai, Zhaoxia and Jin, Guofeng and Sheng, Long
results.abstract: Liposomes are important food-grade delivery systems for hydrophilic and hydrophobic bioactive compounds, but their performance depends on complex interactions among phospholipid source, formulation composition, preparation conditions, and storage environment. These coupled variables make rational design and scalable production challenging. This review summarizes the application of machine learning (ML) across the food liposome value chain, including phospholipid extraction and identification, formulation design, preparation process control, bioactive compound screening, and stability prediction. Particular attention is given to how ML integrates lipid composition, payload properties, and processing parameters to predict key liposome quality attributes, including particle size, polydispersity index, zeta potential, and encapsulation efficiency, thereby guiding formulation optimization. When combined with microfluidic fabrication and automated experimentation, ML can further enhance preparation control and process optimization. Current evidence indicates that ML has strong potential to accelerate food liposome development. This potential arises from its ability to model nonlinear relationships among formulation, processing, and quality attributes and to extract useful information from complex molecular, analytical, imaging, and process datasets. However, current progress remains limited by small and heterogeneous datasets, inconsistent characterization protocols, limited model interpretability, and insufficient transferability across lipid sources, payloads, and food matrices. Future progress will depend on standardized datasets, interpretable models, and closer integration of ML with high-throughput experimentation and validation in real food systems.

results.title: Enhancing heterogeneous multi-agent autonomous exploration in unstructured terrains via dual-layer collaborative control
results.authors: Zhao, Kexiang and Hu, Bingyu and Pan, Yingying and Guo, Chi and Yang, Yuxiang
results.journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society
results.abstract: Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) are of great significance in real-world applications, as they can effectively manage complex tasks through decentralized collaboration. Most existing studies predominantly emphasize homogeneous MAS, i.e., systems consisting of agents with identical functional capabilities and standardized behavioral protocols. However, such systems often fail to adapt effectively to dynamic or disturbed environments during autonomous cooperative exploration. To this end, this paper investigates heterogeneous MAS and introduces a Reinforcement Learning-guided heterogeneous Multi-agent Autonomous Exploration framework (RL-MAE), designed to harness the complementary advantages of diverse agent types. Specifically, the LEP module achieves dynamic distortion pose compensation through a motion correction strategy tailored for heterogeneous platforms, providing a reliable perceptual foundation for task allocation and control. Furthermore, the HDA module establishes a three-level closed-loop architecture spanning planning, navigation, and adaptive coordination, where the upper layer determines target allocation and global paths via MD-MTSP, the middle layer performs local path tracking using TD3, and the lower layer triggers trajectory adjustments via dual-mode cost evaluation only when a cost-reduction condition is satisfied, with the three levels tightly coupled through explicit information feedback. Extensive experiments, including ablation studies, demonstrate that the proposed system achieves superior robustness compared to homogeneous systems in complex unstructured terrain.

results.title: Leveraging the Synergy between Mechanistic Insight and Machine Learning for Predictive Structure-Performance Relationships in Organic Synthesis
results.authors: Sun, Yi-Zhou and Zhang, Shuo-Qing and Hong, Xin
results.abstract: Understanding how molecular structure determines reaction performance is a central objective of physical organic chemistry and an increasingly important challenge in data-driven organic synthesis. As the frontiers of synthetic chemistry continue to advance, predictive structure-performance relationship modeling is expected not only to reproduce known reaction outcomes but also to guide new chemical design. In this Account, we summarize our efforts to integrate mechanistic insight with machine learning across data construction, model development, and discovery applications. At the data level, mechanistic understanding can help define reaction spaces and learning targets, allowing automated density functional theory calculations and literature-derived databases to become chemically consistent learning resources. This idea is illustrated by computed selectivity data sets for radical C-H functionalization and Cu(II)-mediated radical bond formation as well as literature databases for asymmetric hydrogenation of olefins and N,N'-dioxide/metal-catalyzed Michael additions. At the modeling level, mechanistic knowledge can be embedded into reaction representations and model architectures. Transition-state-based reaction encoding introduces pathway-specific stereochemical information into enantioselectivity prediction, while steric- and electronics-embedded molecular graphs incorporate physical organic effects directly into molecular deep learning. At the discovery level, mechanistic relatedness provides a basis for selecting historical data and transferring structure-performance relationships into low-data chemical space. This mechanism-guided transfer learning formalizes how chemists reuse related precedents, enabling few-shot catalyst ligand discovery for Ni-catalyzed atroposelective Suzuki-Miyaura coupling. A central lesson from these studies is that mechanistic insight is not a replacement for machine learning but the chemical foundation that makes it more reliable, interpretable, and extrapolative. By translating mechanistic understanding into data boundaries, reaction representations, and transfer strategies, machine learning can move beyond retrospective fitting and become a chemically grounded framework for predicting and discovering new organic reactions.

results.title: Recent Advances in Graphene-Based Aerogels for Electromagnetic Wave Absorption: A Comprehensive Review
results.authors: Gong, Xiaobin and Wang, Haoran and Zhang, Xinfang and Yang, Leiyu and Dong, Biqin and Zhang, Yuxin
results.abstract: With the rapid development of high-frequency communications, smart electronic devices and aerospace, the problem of electromagnetic interference has become increasingly severe, creating an urgent need for electromagnetic waves (EMWs) absorbing materials that combine high absorption efficiency, broadband response, light weight, and environmental stability. Graphene-based aerogels (GAs) show great promise for EMWs absorption due to their three-dimensional (3D) porous structure, tunable conductivity and surface chemistry, and lightweight high-strength properties. However, existing reviews on EMWs absorbing materials based on GAs have not systematically summarized the synergistic mechanisms between GAs and other materials, nor have they provided an in-depth discussion of optimization strategies for the coordinated regulation of composition and structure. This review comprehensively summarizes the latest research advances in GAs-based EMWs absorbing, explores the fundamental principles of EMWs absorption, and highlights the properties, structural characteristics, and preparation methods of graphene and GAs. In addition, the study examined the effects of defect engineering, multicomponent composites, and structural design (core-shell and heterostructures) on the regulation of EMWs absorption properties. These strategies synergistically yield broad bandwidth and strong attenuation. The review also analyzes the application of GAs in EMWs absorption under special conditions, and discusses the potential use of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning in EMWs absorbing materials. Finally, this review discusses the current challenges and future directions for GA-based EMWs absorbing materials, with the aim of establishing relationships between synthesis, structure, and function, filling gaps in existing reviews, and providing guidance for the future development of EMWs absorbing materials.

results.title: Lesion-Aware Multiple-Instance Learning for Grapevine Disease Recognition from Field RGB Images
results.authors: Öztürk, Övünç and Canbula, Bora and Özacar, Tuğba and Özacar, Vehbi
results.abstract: This retrospective offline study examines how dense manual regional annotations can be organized for image-level grapevine disease recognition using pre-acquired HERMOS RGB images. After audit and filtering, 491 source images and 13,765 Pascal VOC regions were retained. A leakage-safe source-image split was used across full-image classification, regional crop classification, crop-to-image aggregation, annotation-guided multiple-instance learning (MIL), and YOLO11 localization. MIL bags in training, validation, and testing were constructed from crops derived from manual boxes; the results therefore describe annotation-assisted aggregation rather than raw-image deployment. The original ConvNeXt-Tiny MIL model achieved macro-F1 0.922 (95% source-image bootstrap CI 0.882-0.956), compared with 0.836 (0.754-0.895) for full-image ConvNeXt-Tiny and 0.869 (0.804-0.917) for the best fixed crop aggregation. Paired macro-F1 differences favored MIL over these baselines by 0.087 (95% CI 0.029-0.163; Holm-adjusted p = 0.013) and 0.053 (0.005-0.114; adjusted p = 0.036), respectively. Downy mildew precision and recall were 1.000 on nine positive test images, but the corresponding exact 95% binomial intervals were 0.664-1.000. Controlled ablations produced lower point estimates without learned attention or the auxiliary instance loss, whereas removing context expansion did not reduce performance; none of the three paired ablation tests was significant after Holm correction. Increasing detector capacity from YOLO11n to YOLO11s did not improve full-image mAP@0.50 (0.175 versus 0.170). These findings support annotation-guided local-evidence aggregation as an offline exploratory benchmark, while not establishing split-to-split stability, computational efficiency, or external-vineyard generalization.

results.title: Bio-inspired zero-shot learning with hierarchical fault-trait knowledge transfer for cross-domain diagnosis
results.authors: Yang, Qiuyu and Lin, Yuyi and Ruan, Jiangjun and Han, Yun and Xie, Jingyi and Xue, Xue
results.journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society
results.abstract: Fault diagnosis methods for complex mechanical systems often face challenges in adapting to unseen fault types and varying operating conditions. Existing techniques typically suffer from limited cross-domain adaptability and weak zero-shot recognition capabilities. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a bio-inspired zero-shot learning framework that incorporates hierarchical fault-trait knowledge transfer and domain adaptation. A biomimetic network is designed to quantify domain discrepancies and generate transferable domain factors, using a hierarchical fault-trait description framework inspired by the differentiation process from general to specialized features. This approach enables fault diagnosis of previously unseen fault types by leveraging labeled data from the source domain only. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for cross-domain zero-shot diagnosis and suggest its potential applicability to complex mechanical systems.

results.title: When Fever Hides Fire: A Systematic Review of Clinical and Digital Approaches to Early Recognition of Pediatric Sepsis
results.authors: Abdulrahman, Mohammed Elmostafa Khalid and Abdalmagid, Ola Yassir Osman and Almardy, Abdulbagie Musaad Algylani and Mohamed Elhassan, Osman Osama Osman and Abu Haltem, Ibraheem and Ahmed, Asim and Babekr, Nahla Bakri Ageeb
results.abstract: Early recognition of pediatric sepsis remains challenging because clinical presentation, sepsis definitions, and recognition approaches vary across healthcare settings. This systematic review evaluated clinical and digital strategies for the early recognition of pediatric sepsis, including structured screening tools, electronic alerts, prediction models, machine-learning approaches, clinical decision support, and recognition pathways. Diagnostic criteria were considered separately as reference frameworks for classifying established sepsis and interpreting the performance of recognition tools. PubMed and Scopus were systematically searched, eligible studies were independently screened, data were extracted, and methodological quality and risk of bias were assessed using design-appropriate tools. Because of substantial clinical and methodological heterogeneity, the evidence was synthesized narratively. A total of 13 studies were included. Several clinical and digital approaches generally performed well in ruling out sepsis among low-risk children; however, their ability to identify true cases and limit unnecessary alerts varied according to alert thresholds, clinical settings, and the sepsis definition or reference standard used. No single approach was consistently superior for early recognition. Automated screening appeared most useful when integrated with structured clinical assessment rather than used independently. Differences in pediatric sepsis definitions substantially influenced reported performance, and implementation studies more consistently demonstrated improvements in recognition and care processes than in patient outcomes. The available evidence was limited by heterogeneous methods, imperfect reference standards, insufficient external validation, and risk of bias. Clinical and digital recognition systems may support earlier identification of children with suspected infection who require further assessment; however, current evidence does not establish a universally superior approach. Further prospective multicenter studies are needed to determine which strategies provide meaningful clinical benefit across diverse healthcare settings.

results.title: Mind the Gap: A survey of chronic wound datasets, methods, and clinical translation
results.authors: Fatima, Anum and Yap, Moi Hoon and Reeves, Neil D and Odling-Smee, Michael and Bond, David and Kendrick, Connah
results.abstract: Chronic wounds, including diabetic foot ulcers, venous ulcers, arterial ulcers and pressure ulcers, represent a growing global health challenge with significant morbidity, mortality, and economic burden. Advancements in medical image analysis have shown promise in automating wound detection, segmentation, and measurement. However, translation of these research advances into clinical practice through mobile applications remains limited. This survey presents systematic analysis of the relationship between chronic wound datasets, deep learning methods, and mobile wound assessment applications. We analyse 20 datasets (14 public/partially public and 6 private), including iterative challenge datasets that extend image pool through synthetic augmentation. We review 50 deep learning methods spanning encoder-decoder architectures to self-supervised learning approaches, and evaluate 13 mobile applications (commercially deployed clinical tools and research prototypes). We examine the alignment between publicly available chronic wound datasets and the documented capabilities of mobile wound assessment mobile applications. Our analysis reveals critical misalignments between datasets, algorithms and mobile applications. Existing datasets are typically designed for algorithm benchmarking rather than clinical deployment, and therefore lack standardised acquisition protocols, scale calibration markers, depth information, detailed tissue composition annotations, and representation of diverse skin types. Conversely, reviewed mobile applications report capabilities, including automatic tissue classification, calibrated wound measurement and depth estimation, for which publicly available data is insufficient. We map documented dataset characteristics to capabilities reported among reviewed mobile applications, identify unresolved methodological challenges, and outline key priorities for the field. Based on these insights, we propose actionable recommendations for developing clinically translatable computer vision system for wound assessment. This survey is intended to serve as a reference for researchers and practitioners seeking to bridge the gap between medical imaging methodologies and practical demands of clinical wound care.

results.title: Multicenter Evaluation of a Deep Learning Model for Automatic Contouring of Cardiac Substructures in Adults
results.authors: Moignier, Alexandra and Licha, Axel and Felici, Felix and Duverge, Loig and Lange, Martin and Ah-Thiane, Loic and Delpon, Gregory and Karlhede, Anna and Löfman, Fredrik and Skarf, Frida and Söderberg, Jonas and Martin-Mervoyer, Elvire and Thillays, François and Beddok, Arnaud and Vaugier, Loig
results.abstract: PURPOSE: Efficient delineation of cardiac substructures is essential for assessing radiation-induced cardiac toxicity in thoracic radiotherapy. We clinically evaluated a deep learning model designed for automated segmentation of these structures. METHODS AND MATERIALS: The model built in collaboration with XXX (XXX) generated 21 cardiac substructures (whole heart, chambers, coronary arteries, valves, and great vessels). Five radiation oncologists rated raw contours on thirty contrast-enhanced CTs from two institutions using a 4-point Likert scale (3 = no correction, 2 = minor/moderate correction, 1 = major correction, 0 = not performed) and applied corrections when needed. Dice Similarity Coefficients (DSC) and 95th-percentile Hausdorff distances (HD95) were computed to compare model versus reference contours, clinician-corrected versus reference contours, and model versus STAPLE contours. RESULTS: Of 630 structures, 93.8% were scored either 3 or ≥2, and 6.2% received 1 by at least one clinician. For the coronary arteries (210 structures), 88.5% were scored either 3 or ≥ 2. Contour generation took approximately 1 min, with a median review and correction time of 7.0 min per CT (IQR, 5.8-9.8). The median DSC between the model and reference contours was 1.0 across all structures, while it ranged from 0.92 to 1.0 for clinician-corrected versus reference contours. Overall, HD95 was below 5 mm, for both clinicians versus reference and model versus STAPLE. CONCLUSIONS: The deep learning model provided satisfactory segmentation of cardiac substructures on contrast-enhanced CT, including coronary arteries. Its integration into a widely adopted treatment planning system lays the foundation for broad clinical implementation.

results.title: Towards scalable cancer prognosis by aligning semi-supervised learning with survival modeling
results.authors: Huang, Yi and Cai, Linghan and Feng, Ziliang and Zhao, Mengjie and Tu, Xiaoguang and Yuan, Zhiyuan and Wang, Zhikang
results.abstract: Prognostic assessment via whole-slide images (WSIs) is a key task in computational pathology. However, the development of robust predictive models is often bottlenecked by the scarcity of survival-annotated data, given the longitudinal nature of clinical follow-up. Despite its potential, semi-supervised learning (SSL) remains underexplored in this field. Existing SSL methods, primarily designed for natural image classification, rely on the assumption of marginally independent categories, which makes them difficult to adapt to the high-dimensional complexity of WSIs and the temporal continuity inherent in survival outcomes. To bridge this gap, we propose a novel semi-supervised multiple instance learning (MIL) framework tailored for WSI-based prognosis. Specifically, we first introduce a morphology-perceived MIL network (Morph-MIL) that jointly models tissue composition and global semantic representations. To maintain a stable reference, a dynamic memory bank is employed to encapsulate the multi-level representations of labeled samples (censored & uncensored). Furthermore, we develop a pseudo-labeling strategy that assigns discrete labels containing temporal relationships to annotation-free data by aligning their features with the memory bank through bin-wise aggregation. Comprehensive evaluation establishes the superiority of the proposed framework, while extensive ablation analyses and visualizations confirm its efficacy in prognostic prediction and biological interpretation. Consequently, this study offers a scalable solution for WSI survival modeling in scenarios with limited annotations. The code is available at: https://github.com/yihuangswust-alt/SSL-Morph_MIL.

results.title: Force-regulated robotic diffuse reflectance spectroscopy scanning
results.authors: Deng, Kaizhong and Zhou, Zhangxi and Giot, Maxime and Gkouzionis, Ioannis and Peters, Christopher and Mylonas, George and Elson, Daniel
results.abstract: SIGNIFICANCE: Intraoperative discrimination between malignant and benign tissue is essential for achieving complete tumor resection while preserving healthy structures. Robotic diffuse reflectance spectroscopy (DRS) enables automated intraoperative tissue assessment, but unregulated probe-tissue contact forces introduce spectral artifacts and risk tissue damage, limiting clinical translation. AIM: We present and evaluate an autonomous robotic DRS scanning system incorporating real-time contact force regulation to enable safe, repeatable, and large-area ex vivo tissue assessment. APPROACH: A serial robot manipulator equipped with a fiber-optic DRS probe, load cell, and camera employed hybrid visual servoing and force feedback control, maintaining 0.08 N target force with < 0.30    N  peak limits. Performance was evaluated on ex vivo bovine and ovine tissues including scanning safety, force regulation versus expert operators, spectral consistency across six novice operators, and tissue classification using support vector machines. RESULTS: The system achieved 100% and 93% scan completion rates on bovine and ovine tissues, respectively, without visible tissue damage. Autonomous operation enabled 46 continuous trials over ∼ 30    min  without human intervention. Mean applied force (0.079 N) matched manual sampling (0.080 N) with reduced variance and lower peak forces. Robotic spectral acquisitions aligned with manual measurements, yielding mean inter-observer spectral angles of 1.43 deg, comparable to inter-human operator variability. Tissue classification demonstrated high discriminatory accuracy in bench-top validation. CONCLUSIONS: Force-regulated robotic DRS enables standardized, autonomous tissue scanning with expert-level spectral consistency, advancing spectroscopic sensing toward reliable automated surgical margin assessment.

results.title: Objective quantification of suckling biomechanics in infants with and without tongue-tie using hydraulic differential-pressure recording and machine learning
results.authors: Siggaard, Lene Dahl and Chiriaev, Serguei and Knudsen, Anders Kramer and Lildholdt, Torben
results.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Objective assessment of infant suckling biomechanics remains limited despite decades of pressure-based measurement research, and tongue-tie (ankyloglossia) is still largely evaluated using semi-quantitative anatomical scoring. We developed a hydraulic differential-pressure device - the electronic baby bottle (EBB) - designed to record real-time net intraoral mechanical load during nutritive suckling through a fluid-filled sensing cavity with a controlled air inclusion coupled to a differential pressure transducer. This study aimed to: (1) describe the EBB measurement principle, (2) develop automated machine learning-based classification of effective suckling activity, and (3) evaluate whether quantitative biomechanical parameters derived from automated analysis demonstrate responsiveness one week after frenotomy. METHODS: Time-series recordings from iterative prototype testing were segmented into overlapping windows and manually annotated to train a supervised classifier using the ROCKET transform implemented in Python (sktime) with ridge classification and cross-validation. Performance was evaluated on an internal held-out test set and an independent external validation set of full-length recordings excluded from model development. Quantitative parameters were computed from automatically identified effective suckling bursts in 25 infants with restrictive tongue-tie recorded before and one week after frenotomy and compared with 10 control infants with normal tongue mobility. RESULTS: Automated classification achieved >99% accuracy on the internal test set and 92% segment-level classification accuracy on external validation recordings. Mean negative intraoral pressure during effective suckling bursts increased in 19/25 (76%) treated infants one week after frenotomy (paired t-test, p = 0.010), shifting toward control values. DISCUSSION: Hydraulic differential-pressure recording combined with time-series machine learning enables objective and reproducible quantification of nutritive suckling activity and detects short-term functional change following frenotomy in most infants with restrictive tongue-tie. This framework supports future work on normative reference ranges, standardized digital metrics, and data-driven diagnostic thresholds for infant feeding dysfunction.

results.title: Construction of a readmission prediction model and development of a decision support system for chronic heart failure patients based on patient-reported outcome measures
results.authors: Yu, Chen and Lou, Miaomiao and Sun, Yang and Yang, Zhe and Zhu, Liang
results.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To construct a readmission risk prediction model for heart failure based on an Automated Machine Learning (AutoML) framework and develop a Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) integrating Patient-Reported Outcome Measures (PROM), aiming to address the limitations of traditional models in processing multidimensional physiological-psychological-social data and their low clinical translation efficiency. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study design was employed, enrolling 552 chronic heart failure patients (training-to-testing set ratio of 8:2). Multidimensional features were collected via electronic medical records and the Chinese version of the Heart Failure-Specific PROM Scale (CHF-PROM). Missing data were handled using Multivariate Imputation by Chained Equations (MICE). An AutoML framework driven by an Improved Pied Kingfisher Optimizer (IPKO) algorithm, integrating algorithms including Logistic Regression, Support vector machine (SVM), XGBoost, and LightGBM, was developed. Model performance and interpretability were evaluated using the Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC), Decision Curve Analysis (DCA), and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). A visualized decision-making tool was implemented on the MATLAB platform. RESULTS: Testing set showed the AutoML model achieved significantly enhanced predictive efficacy [AUC = 0.8909, 95% Confidence Interval (CI): 0.8392 to 0.9426]. SHAP analysis revealed key multidimensional factors influencing prognosis, among which milder depressive symptoms, higher levels of social support, and favorable appetite-sleep status were important protective factors reducing readmission risk, while female sex and advanced age were identified as risk predictors. Decision curve analysis further confirmed that applying this model yielded positive net clinical benefit across a wide risk threshold range of 1.2% to 78.6%. CONCLUSION: This study achieved efficient translation of PROM data into clinical decisions and innovatively demonstrated the independent predictive value of psychosocial factors for readmission. The developed CDSS system provides a feasible pathway for the proactive prevention and management of heart failure.

results.title: A target amplification-free CRISPR biosensor with digital microfluidic processing for microRNA profiling in AI-enhanced pediatric sepsis diagnosis
results.authors: Huang, Di and Shi, Shanshan and Wang, Xitong and Li, Wei and Zhang, Xianghong and Xiang, Wenqing and Xu, Zhipeng and He, Yichen and Shen, Peijie and Fang, Xiangming and Xu, Zhinan
results.abstract: MicroRNA signatures provide an informative readout of host-response dysregulation in pediatric sepsis, but their clinical translation remains limited by low target abundance and multiplexing requirements. Here, a target amplification-free CRISPR biosensing platform was established. The sensing mechanism couples Cas13a target recognition to promoter release, template reconstruction, and transcription-driven Cas13a reactivation, enabling fluorescence amplification through internal molecular cycling without amplifying the target miRNAs. Then, an electrowetting-based digital microfluidic chip was designed to compartmentalize parallel reactions and automate droplet generation, reaction assembly, isothermal incubation, magnetic separation, and fluorescence readout. Under optimized conditions, four sepsis-associated biomarkers (miR-15a, miR-21, miR-146a, and miR-155) and the reference control (snRNA U44) were detected at attomolar levels (expected mean input of 1.67 molecules per reaction) with good specificity and minimal inter-droplet interference. The resulting miRNA profiles were then used as input features for machine learning-enhanced sepsis classification and risk assessment. In 252 clinical samples, the resulting model achieved a test-set AUC of 0.973 and an overall accuracy of 92.1%. The model-derived risk score was associated with the Phoenix Sepsis Score and, in a representative longitudinal case, showed preliminary potential to reflect disease evolution. Overall, this platform enables automated analysis of disease-associated miRNA signatures and demonstrates its potential for in-vitro diagnosis of pediatric sepsis.

results.title: Deep learning applications in parasite microscopy: A scoping review
results.authors: Maniraj, Rose Mary and Osman, Emelia and Sheikh Abdullah, Siti Norul Huda and Azil, Aishah Hani and Mahmud, Mohd Amierul Fikri
results.abstract: BACKGROUND: Parasitic diseases remain a significant contributor to the global burden of disease and conventional microscopy remains the gold standard for parasite detection. However, it is labour-intensive and dependent on skilled personnel, leading to variability in diagnostic accuracy. Recent advances in deep learning have enabled automated analysis of microscopy images, offering potential improvements in diagnostic efficiency and consistency. METHODOLOGY/PRINCIPAL FINDINGS: This scoping review aimed to map current evidence on deep learning applications in parasite microscopy for human clinical diagnosis. A systematic search of seven electronic databases was conducted for studies published between January 2015 and July 2025. Eligible studies included primary research that applied deep learning models to parasite microscopy images and reported performance metrics. A total of 118 studies were included. Image classification was the most commonly reported task, followed by object detection, while image segmentation was less frequently investigated. A wide range of architectures was used, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs), YOLO-based detection models and hybrid approaches. Most studies reported high performance across tasks, however, direct comparison was limited due to heterogeneity in datasets, evaluation metrics and experimental designs. In addition, most studies relied on internal validation using subsets of the same dataset, with limited external validation. Among the studies included in this review, several proposed implementation strategies. However, relatively few reported implementation or evaluation in real-world clinical or diagnostic laboratory settings. CONCLUSIONS/SIGNIFICANCE: Deep learning demonstrates substantial potential for automated parasite detection in microscopy. Among the studies included in this review, most deep learning models were evaluated under experimental conditions, with relatively few reporting implementation or evaluation in clinical or diagnostic laboratory settings. Key challenges include dataset heterogeneity, lack of standardised evaluation and limited real-world validation. Future research should prioritise external validation and implementation-focused studies to support integration into clinical and laboratory workflows.

results.title: Practical applications of computational pathology: bridging technology and clinical practice
results.authors: Hanna, Matthew G and Rashidi, Hooman and Pantanowitz, Liron
results.abstract: Computational pathology, driven by advances in artificial intelligence and digital imaging, is rapidly reshaping how pathology data are interpreted and utilised in clinical settings. By leveraging machine learning models and pathology text, tabular, molecular, and imaging data, these technologies offer practical solutions to support routine diagnostics, workflow optimisation, quality assurance, and personalised patient care. From automated screening and triage to diagnostic decision support and prognostic modelling, computational tools are increasingly being evaluated for integration into the pathologist's toolkit. Despite clear potential, real-world adoption remains uneven, and the evidence base is still limited by retrospective study designs, small or enriched cohorts, variable external validation, model generalisability across scanners and institutions, clinical integration, reimbursement, and regulatory authorisation. Addressing these issues requires access to diverse datasets, collaborative model development, analytical and clinical validation using real-world data, robust deployment infrastructure, post-deployment monitoring, and education for end-users. This review explores the current landscape of computational pathology with a focus on actionable clinical applications. It highlights successful use cases, critically appraises common barriers to adoption, and outlines key steps to translate technological advances into clinical value. By bridging the divide between innovation and implementation, computational pathology has the potential to become a vital component of modern diagnostic medicine.

results.title: ADMET all-inclusive: Accountability for the full end-to-end model life cycle is key to success
results.authors: Kuhnke, Lara and Göller, Andreas H
results.abstract: Drug discovery requires balancing efficacy with pharmacokinetic and safety properties. Although machine learning models for ADMET (absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion and toxicology) prediction are increasingly sophisticated, their impact is often limited by challenges in deployment, user adoption, interpretability and project-specific applicability. In this perspective, we describe Bayer's predicTeam approach, which assumes end-to-end responsibility for the prediction lifecycle, from endpoint selection and data curation to deployment, user training and performance monitoring. Key elements include close collaboration with experimental scientists, automated retraining workflows, structured user education and project-specific applicability reports. Drawing on more than a decade of experience, we argue that data quality, curation, governance and organizational accountability are often more important for impact than algorithmic innovation alone, particularly as AI-driven drug discovery continues to evolve.

results.title: Automated integration of spatial location and eye gaze tracking: An extensible multimodal system for developmental data
results.authors: Rothenburger, Bastian and Liang, Yibiao and Schaumlöffel, Timothy and Roig, Gemma and Shing, Yee Lee
results.abstract: Advances in computer vision and mobile sensing enable the study of development in naturalistic environments, yet existing motion tracking systems lack the integration of automated analysis and accessibility needed in developmental research. Current approaches force trade-offs between precision and ecological validity, requiring structured protocols that constrain spontaneous interactions or manual coding that cannot scale for large-scale studies of individual differences. We present an integrated system combining high-density data collection with machine learning-supported analysis using off-the-shelf components. The architecture integrates ceiling-mounted cameras, Pupil Labs eye trackers, and recording hardware, synchronized via Lab Streaming Layer (LSL) protocol with millisecond precision. The modular architecture supports deployment in freely designed environments and can be extended with additional LSL-compatible sensors. Ceiling-mounted cameras operate unobtrusively without requiring wearables, addressing key feasibility challenges in infant and toddler research. The automated pipeline employs off-the-shelf computer vision models for person detection and tracking, with vision-language models distinguishing children from caregivers without manual annotation. The system integrates spatial positioning with eye tracking data, and prototype-based object detection identifies researcher-specific stimuli through reference photographs rather than custom model training. We demonstrate deployment feasibility with toddler-caregiver dyads (from 24 months of age) in free play and validate system accuracy across an extended age range (24 to 63 months). Children tolerated the equipment well, and the pipeline extracted high-density behavioral metrics without manual coding. This system enables scalable measurement of unconstrained early behavior, addressing a methodological gap constraining developmental research.

results.title: Robust disturbance-aware actor-critic reinforcement learning for multi-DOF robotic manipulators
results.authors: Nguyen, Viet Ngu and Le, Thi Minh Tam and Pham, Duc Hung and Nguyen, Huu Cuong
results.abstract: Building on recent insights that augmenting reinforcement-learning policies with disturbance estimates improves robustness and sim-to-real transfer, this paper proposes a disturbance-aware actor-critic RL framework for high-precision robotic manipulators. We derive the dynamics of manipulators ranging from two to six degrees of freedom and design a nonlinear disturbance observer that provides real-time estimates of lumped uncertainties. Unlike conventional feedforward-only designs, the proposed DACRL framework deeply integrates DOB information into the actor-critic's learning state, cost function, and update laws to explicitly compensate for unknown dynamics and disturbances. A Lyapunov-based analysis proves that tracking errors, observer errors and neural-network weight errors remain uniformly ultimately bounded. Extensive simulations show that the proposed controller achieves sub-degree tracking errors across multiple DOF cases, with the 2-DOF example achieving steady-state errors below ±0.02 rad (Joint 1) and ±0.05 rad (Joint 2) and delivering faster convergence and smoother torques than conventional RL and DOB baselines. The disturbance-aware controller generalizes across trajectories and payloads, offering improved robustness while retaining learning flexibility. While the current study focuses on performance and robustness, future work could explore the integration of disturbance-observer-based control barrier functions to formally address safety constraints during the learning process. Simulation results suggest that the disturbance-aware controller can improve robustness while retaining learning flexibility. Real-platform validation remains an important direction for future work.

results.title: Genome-scale metabolic models enable predictive strain and process design for sustainable biomanufacturing
results.authors: Xu, Shuai-Shuai and Ding, Ji and Chen, Shu-Yi and Li, Yu-Chen and Wan, Jia-Yi and Mo, Li and Liu, He and Xu, Qing
results.abstract: Genome-scale metabolic models (GEMs) have emerged as powerful tools for optimizing microbial fermentation. This review traces the application of GEMs from model reconstruction through to industrial implementation. Automated reconstruction tools including CarveMe, ModelSEED, and RAVEN are discussed alongside quality-control frameworks such as MEMOTE. Biological validation of these models ultimately depends on comparing predicted phenotypes against experimental data. The review then focuses on how GEMs guide strain engineering and process optimization, enabling rational target identification, improved substrate utilization, and enhanced fermentation performance. The predictive accuracy and experimental validation of these applications vary considerably across microbial hosts and production contexts. Recent methodological advances, including machine learning-assisted model refinement, synthetic pathway design, and community-scale metabolic modeling, have extended the scope and predictive power of GEMs still further. Persistent challenges in model accuracy, data integration, and scale-up validation remain, yet continued progress in computational and experimental approaches is expected to solidify the role of GEMs in fermentation research and bioprocess development.

results.title: Identifying Family Relationships from Electronic Health Records: A Machine Learning Approach
results.authors: Pundir, Abhinav and Hill, Andrew and Kahn, Michael G and Kwan, Bethany M and Lindberg, Daniel M and Grannis, Shaun J and Schleyer, Titus K and Schilling, Lisa M and Kautz, Sarah V and Ong, Toan C
results.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
results.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To develop and evaluate machine learning methods for automated identification of family relationships from electronic health records (EHRs). We employed Random Forest classifiers to identify five relationship types: Mother-Child, Father-Child, Sibling-Sibling, Twin-Twin, and Partner-Partner, using a four-stage iterative refinement process to improve precision for patient-centered outcomes research (PCOR) and healthcare applications. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We used two large-scale Indiana datasets: the Indiana Network for Patient Care (INPC), comprising approximately 15 million unique individuals across approximately 45 million medical records, and the Indiana Natality dataset (birth certificates, 1970-2024), which served as the gold standard. Positive cases were derived by linking verified relationships from Natality records to INPC using a shared Global Identifier. Negative cases were drawn from a three-tier blocking strategy combined with sliding window restriction and similarity scoring, which together reduced the comparison space from over 1017 potential pairs to approximately 121 million candidates. Five Random Forest classifiers underwent four-stage iterative refinement: initial training, feature removal for multicollinearity, feature engineering to address systematic errors, and training-data refinement restricted to relationship pairs with at least one shared contact feature. RESULTS: The models achieved precision of 0.92 to 1.00, recall of 0.97 to 1.00, and F1 scores of 0.94 to 1.00 across all relationship types (Mother-Child 0.97, Father-Child 0.98, Sibling-Sibling 0.98, Twin-Twin 1.00, Partner-Partner 0.94). Between 15% and 78% of Natality-verified relationships lacked any shared contact information in INPC and were structurally undetectable by record linkage; restricting training and evaluation to linkable pairs improved precision for four of the five models, and training-data refinement improved F1-scores by a further 0.02-0.04 for the Mother-Child, Father-Child, and Sibling models. High-confidence predictions (probability ≥ 0.9) captured 77-99% of true positives. Age difference was the primary predictor for parent-child and twin relationships, while phone number similarity was most important for siblings. DISCUSSION: The framework identifies family relationships from standard demographic fields available in most EHR systems. The iterative refinement approach shows how systematic error analysis can guide methodological improvements. Training-data refinement addresses a constraint in EHR-based family linkage: not all verified biological relationships have overlapping demographic footprints in healthcare data. Unlike rule-based approaches, the framework provides probability scores that enable configurable deployment thresholds. CONCLUSION: The Random Forest models demonstrate high performance suitable for large-scale research deployment and are ready for testing in clinical applications rather than immediate widespread clinical use. The methodology can be adapted to other EHR systems, supporting family-centered study design in patient-centered outcomes research.

results.title: Context-aware asymmetric ensembling for interpretable retinopathy of prematurity screening via active query and vascular attention
results.authors: Hassan, Md Mehedi and Hasan, Taufiq
results.abstract: Retinopathy of Prematurity (ROP) is among the major causes of preventable childhood blindness. Automated screening remains challenging, primarily due to limited data availability and the complexity of the condition involving both structural staging and microvascular abnormalities. Current deep learning models depend heavily on large private datasets and passive multimodal fusion, which commonly fail to generalize to small, imbalanced public cohorts. We thus propose the Context-Aware Asymmetric Ensemble Model (CAA Ensemble) that simulates clinical reasoning through two specialized streams.
